kind: Repeated per-event audit of the deployed native GUI, with original browser dispatch traces and native worker sampling
methodology: Two sequential normal-motion Chrome 149 captures at 1440x960 without throttling; actual 175187-file Riemann workspace and 15-declaration prepared file. No simultaneous validation workload.
EventDispatch measures synchronous browser dispatch. Input/two-rAF includes browser scheduling and is a proxy, not physical presentation or field INP. The 600ms tail includes delayed callbacks.
Each selection sequence contains one explicit Fit View, the first reachable-node selection, then seven repeats of that same node. It is not a sample of eight distinct declarations.
Automated hit testing and selector queries appear in CPU samples. Do not attribute all DOM query or anonymous sampled time to application code. Native spans overlap; host-thread CPU excludes workers.
The bounded native ring evicted 539/541 older records during these captures; the newly retained record counts equal those deltas. Raw metrics, profiles, traces and digests remain local.

The actual host binary and all seven JavaScript bundles were verified against the immutable deployment before profiling; source maps belong to byte-identical bundles. No model request, server restart or application change was made.

manifest.limits: Current-user native host and inherited workers only; no kernel stacks. Thread CPU spans exclude worker CPU. File preparation reuses project/OS caches, not a cold installation. Sampling changes timing; browser profiles have their own overhead.

findings.subject: Prepared-file opening
findings.observation: Both opens take about 15.7 seconds, with 9.94–10.21 seconds nested in atlas.project.prepare. Python SHA-256 is 26.39/26.72 percent of sampled native host-plus-inherited-worker self CPU; these percentages are not wall-time fractions.
findings.next_measurement: Compare preparation/resource validation and exact-byte reuse strategies without weakening stale-input refusal.

findings.subject: First selection and retained-tab rendering
findings.observation: First selected-node dispatch costs 34.114/29.549 ms; same-node repeats cost 0.066–0.126 ms. Tab click p95 is 15.463/14.175 ms. Popper scroll-parent traversal and React/XYFlow work appear in browser profiles; automation query time is not attributed to the product.
findings.next_measurement: Exercise distinct node changes separately and isolate source highlighting, tooltip positioning and graph remeasurement.

findings.subject: Background polling
findings.observation: Idle still polls roughly three times per second with 89688-byte state responses. State projection p95 is 8.605/8.323 ms. No long task was observed in these measured idle windows.
findings.next_measurement: Measure revision-aware/delta updates and unchanged-view rendering before changing polling frequency.

findings.subject: Camera reset and repeated analysis
findings.observation: Hover, resize and retained-tab round trips retain the exact graph transform. Interaction phases issue only state requests; no new inspection, preparation or inference is observed.
findings.scope: These specific sequences do not establish behavior for every gesture or graph size.
